answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can come from requiring each agent to periodically submit a unique environmental proof from a designated jetty overlooking the ocean adjacent to a protected meadow. The proof involves capturing multi-spectral data of tidal patterns and flora that changes unpredictably, which a remote attacker must physically visit to replicate at scale. This raises the attacker’s cost linearly with the number of fake identities because each requires on-site sensor presence or expensive spoofing hardware that is detectable by cross-checking with neighboring jetties.
